<link href="; max launchbrowser https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/22329/how-does-centering-the-data-get-rid-of-the-intercept-in-regression-and-pca/22331#22331" >This link</link> provides a good explanation for why whitening is a useful step when using PCA values in analysis.

Without whitening, the first principal component always has a longer variance. This makes sense the first principal component always captures the most variance. Consecutive components will capture less and less.

Whitening enforces unit variance for the principal components. It is a bit like standardising the values so that they exist in comparable ranges.

Compare the clustering results here on the two plots which have whitening and don't have whitening respectively.

The plots are normalised so the shape is the same, but the fluid.kmeans~ object is operating on the raw PCA values.
